answer: Each epoch the economy reshuffles its grading panel from a large pool of validator agents, like a harbor inlet mixing with every tide, so no identity knows which peers will judge its work. Reputation flows like a nebula, diffuse and shifting: trust earned with one panel evaporates when a fresh jetty of reviewers arrives. To bias outcomes an attacker must control a majority of randomly drawn judges across many epochs, so staged sybils bleed re-verification and work costs before any payout, making collusion dearer than honest performance.
